title: 162 Effects of cattle hide color and changing environmental conditions at northern latitudes on feeder cattle performance and behavior
content:
Abstract
Although research has explored the influence of climatic conditions on feeder cattle welfare, limited studies examine the relationship between hide color (albedo) and cattle thermoregulation in response to extreme environmental changes, particularly of those seen at northern latitudes. Therefore, the objective of this study is to evaluate feeder cattle performance in response to environmental conditions and hide color. Angus-based yearling steers (n=47; averaging 405.81kg) were stratified by weight and hide color (Red, White, and Black) and, within stratum, randomly assigned to the following four treatment groups; 1) Black Angus, 2) Black Sim/Angus, 3) Red Angus, and 4) White Charolais/Angus steers. For the 140 day finishing period, twelve feedlot pens were used (3 pens per treatment) with each pen having two Vytelle electronic feed bunks equipped with an antenna to detect animal presence, load cells to measure feed disappearance and wireless transfer to a data-acquisition computer. Finishing diet (9.3% CP, 80% TDN) consisted of 69% corn, 21% corn silage, 10% wheat straw, and 0.45 kg per head per day of beef grower pellet with a fortified mineral and vitamin package. Initial and final unshrunk weights were obtained on two consecutive days and averaged. Every 28d, steers were weighed prior to feeding, a measurement of coat depth and tag score was estimated. Animal surface temperature was recorded via a FLIR E5xt thermal imaging camera on the same day of every week at 0730 (prior to feeding) and 1330 (6 hrs. post feeding) for 20 weeks. There was a treatment by period interaction in hair depth (P≤0.01), with red hided steers having the longest hair length at 28d (P≤0.02) with no differences recorded for other periods (P>0.10). Treatment and period effect (P≤0.02) on average daily gain (ADG), however post hoc means separation showed no difference in ADG (P≥0.24). Tag score displayed a treatment by period interaction (P≤0.01), with Black Angus having greater tag scores in period 3 than Black Sim/Angus and Red Angus (P≤0.01) but not White Charolais/Angus steers (P=0.44). Hide color had no impact (P=0.99) on morning surface temperatures of the steers. However, there was a period effect on steer surface temperatures in the morning (P≤0.01), with period 1 temperatures differing from period 5 temperatures (P≤0.05). There was a treatment by period interaction (P≤0.01), where the first 3 periods Red Angus steers had greater temperatures than White Charolais/Angus steers (P≤0.01), and in periods 4 and 5 Red Angus and White Charolais/Angus had similar temperatures (P≥0.43). Black Angus and Black Sim/Angus steers always had warmer surface temperatures than White Charolais/Angus steers (P≤0.02). In summary, there was an environmental effect on steer albedo, which in turn may help explain changes observed with period/treatment effects on ADG, hair length, and tag score.
